$comment: SEO/GEO target-query backlog. This is the system of record for what the content agent writes next and why. Every entry carries the evidence that justified it: who actually ranked when it was last checked, and on which engine. Update `evidence` when you re-run the audit; never add a query without checking what already wins it, because the winning page format is the single most useful thing the SERP tells you.
$demandStudy: tq-011 to tq-020 come from GEO-Tracking/Keyword-Demand-Study-2026-08-26.md. Entries with `evidence.checked: null` were justified on demand data only and still need a SERP check before writing, which report.mjs will tell you.

clusters.training: Someone wants their team taught to use AI. Highest commercial intent for Traq.
clusters.strategy: Someone wants help deciding what to do with AI before buying or training. Nazir's stated buyer intent.
clusters.activation: Someone already pays for AI tools and is getting nothing back. Traq's sharpest wedge.
clusters.consulting: Generic AI consulting demand, most contested, mostly won by directories.
clusters.comparison: Evaluation-stage queries. Highest AI-citation rate of any format (~33%).
clusters.local: UAE/Dubai-qualified variants. Winnable because the competitor set is small and weak.
clusters.pricing: Someone is budgeting or comparing quotes. Largest coherent cluster in the 2026-08-26 demand study, and the winning format is unambiguous: the number and the year go in the title tag.
clusters.vertical: Someone wants AI help for their specific industry or role. Long-tail and low-competition, and it is the shape of question people ask an AI assistant rather than Google.
clusters.compliance: Someone has to buy training because a regulation says so. Mandated demand rather than discretionary.

queries.query: AI training company Dubai for corporate teams
queries.note: Traq has a service page but it does not rank. The pages that win are geo-qualified with named formats, durations and prices. The existing page has none of those.

evidence.observation: Every winner names the geography in the H1 and publishes a course/format list. None of them are better practitioners. They are more specific.

queries.note: Position 4 on this query is Clutch's own Dubai AI list, which Traq is on but at page 2. Winning here is as much an off-domain job as an on-domain one. See outreach-targets.json.

evidence.observation: A directory list and a Quora thread both outrank every independent provider site. Third-party surfaces beat owned surfaces on this query.

queries.query: who should I hire to train my team to use AI in Dubai
queries.note: This is the conversational form buyers actually use with an AI assistant, and it is the exact prompt Traq lost on. Write the guide that answers it honestly, including how to brief and evaluate a provider, because that is the passage an engine will lift.

evidence.observation: ChatGPT's own stated filter was 'boutiques beat big academies for a 20-person firm because they map real workflows'. That is Traq's positioning verbatim. It recommended six other firms purely because Traq was in none of the sources it read.

queries.query: how to build an AI strategy for a small business
queries.note: Named by Nazir as core buyer intent. Top-of-funnel but it feeds every commercial query underneath it. Needs a real step sequence, not a definition.

evidence.observation: Every winner publishes a numbered step sequence (identify pain points, pick a use case, pilot, measure, scale), not a definition. Shopify and Salesforce are the only two written specifically for small businesses; the rest are enterprise-generic. Matched the format with a six-step guide plus a one-page worksheet table instead of prose.

queries.query: how to get value from AI tools we already pay for
queries.note: Traq's sharpest differentiator and the one nobody else is targeting. Named by Nazir. Variants worth covering in the same guide: 'nobody uses the AI tools we bought', 'low Copilot adoption', 'we pay for ChatGPT and nobody uses it'.

evidence.observation: No page targets this exact query. The SERP is generic enterprise adoption-strategy content (Copilot rollout guides, change-management blogs) aimed at large enterprises, none framed as auditing a tool already bought. Confirms the note: underserved, most content sells a new tool rather than activating one already paid for.

queries.note: Pricing pages get cited disproportionately because AI answers want concrete numbers. Publish real ranges even if banded. Refusing to name a number is why vendors get skipped in AI answers.

evidence.observation: Same two pages still surface three-plus weeks later. sawankr.com still publishes explicit AED price bands per workshop format (half-day, full-day, multi-day); parikshitkhanna.com remains quote-only with no public figure. Matched the winning format by leading the new guide with the same real AED bands, sourced and cited rather than invented.

queries.query: AI training vs AI consulting: which does my team need
queries.note: Comparison articles are roughly a third of all AI citations. Traq already has 'AI consultant vs AI agency'; this is the adjacent gap and it maps directly onto the two services.

evidence.observation: Must stay genuinely balanced. Obviously self-serving comparisons get filtered out of AI answers.

queries.query: how to make AI training stick after a workshop
queries.note: The control experiment. Traq owns a matching article and lost anyway, because the note had zero content headings. Headings were added 2026-07-31, so if this query is still lost after a recrawl, on-site structure is not the constraint and effort should move entirely off-domain.

evidence.observation: Winners are not more authoritative than Traq. They are more structured: multi-heading guides against Traq's flat 475-word block.

queries.query: best AI training companies in Dubai
queries.note: Deliberately NOT an on-domain target. This query is won by listicles, and a self-published 'best of' listing yourself first is both weak and correctly distrusted by AI engines. The job is to get onto other people's lists. See outreach-targets.json.

evidence.observation: Several Perplexity citations traced to a Bayut listicle, a property portal. One well-placed third-party list outperformed every provider's own site.

queries.note: Long-tail, low competition, high intent, and precisely what Traq delivers. Cheap win once the higher-priority items ship.

Highest single buyer-intent term in the whole demand harvest and Traq has nothing on it. Publish real bands the way the corporate-training-cost guide already does, but for consulting engagements, and put the range in the title.

evidence.observation: Checked through the adjacent query 'how much does an AI consultant cost per hour'. Every page-one result carries a price range AND the year in the title tag. Not one of them asks the question; they all answer it in the title.

demand.note: Prominence is an inverse-rank tally across locales, not search volume. Related terms: 'ai consultant hourly rate' 8.10, 'ai consultant price per hour' 5.53, 'ai consultant cost' 3.30.

queries.note: Executives search for the people, not the discipline: 'employee ai training' and 'staff ai training' both outrank every abstract term in the harvest. The winning format bundles programs, costs and ROI on one page.

evidence.observation: Top result is titled 'AI Training for Employees (2026): Programs, Costs & ROI'. Costs and the year in the title again. Several winners lead with named company examples (KPMG, PwC, Ally), which Traq cannot match and should not try to; the price transparency is the winnable half.

demand.note: 'employee ai training' 4.50, 'staff ai training' 3.75, 'ai training for employees' 3.00, 'how to train employees on ai' 3.00.

queries.note: Retitled on 2026-08-26 from 'AI training for teams that actually use it' to 'Employee AI Training, Dubai and Abu Dhabi', to use the phrase buyers actually type plus the geo. The page still lacks the named formats, durations and prices that every UAE winner publishes. See tq-001, which is the same gap.

evidence.observation: Carried over from tq-001. The retitle addresses the phrasing half of that finding; the format list is still missing.

demand.note: Geo variants: 'ai training dubai' 8.18, 'ai training uae' 6.43, 'corporate ai training uae' 4.42.

queries.note: In the UAE 'AI course' outdraws 'AI training'; worldwide it is the reverse. The local market searches in the language of structured, credentialed learning, which is exactly why the training institutes win these SERPs. Traq publishes nothing shaped like a course: no named modules, no duration, no outcome list. This is a packaging gap, not a capability gap.

demand.note: Relative interest indexed within one set of five: AI course 61.7, AI training 50.5, AI consulting 9.6, AI consultant 4.0, AI workshop 4.0. Worldwide the same set reads AI training 58.5, AI course 37.0. Also surfaced: 'ai course dubai government' 4.50, which is an untouched public-sector angle.

queries.query: how to use AI in a real estate business
queries.note: The strongest vertical-and-geo overlap available to Traq: real estate is one of Dubai's largest sectors and it has real searched AI demand. Zero coverage on the site today. Write it for an agency principal, not a developer.

demand.note: Indexed within one set of five verticals: AI for healthcare 37.4, AI for real estate 32.0, AI for HR 14.6, AI for lawyers 5.6, AI for accountants 1.6. Not comparable to the head-term sets.

queries.note: Highest-scoring role vertical in the autocomplete harvest. The exact phrasing matters here: 'AI training for accountants' is a real query while 'AI for accountants' as a general topic is not, so write to the long-tail phrase verbatim.

demand.note: Against Trends 'AI for accountants' at 1.6 in the vertical set. The two disagree and both are right: the demand lives in the long-tail phrasing, not the topic. Related: 'ai consulting for accounting' 3.75, 'how to use ai for cost accounting' 4.00.

queries.note: Second-strongest role vertical, and it scores independently on the consulting phrasing too. Confidentiality and privilege are the objections to lead with, which suits Traq's guardrails angle.

demand.note: 'ai consulting for law firms' scored 4.00 separately. Trends 'AI for lawyers' 5.6 in the vertical set.

queries.note: Mandated demand rather than discretionary, which makes it a different sale entirely. Applies to any UAE client with EU operations, customers or staff, and to Traq's remote worldwide delivery. Check the current text of the obligation before writing; do not state a deadline from memory.

demand.note: Trends 'AI literacy' 6.1 against 'prompt engineering course' 1.0 in the same set. Autocomplete returns 'ai literacy training for employees', 'ai literacy training eu', 'ai literacy training ireland', 'ai literacy training uk'.

queries.note: The guide already exists and is good. It is titled 'How to write an AI use policy for a small business' while the searched phrase is 'ai policy for companies'. Retitle toward the query and add a downloadable one-page template rather than writing a second page.

demand.note: Also 'ai policy for nonprofits' 1.50, which suggests a sector-templated version has legs.
